title: Spectral Collapse Drives Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning
claim: Standard training collapses the curvature spectrum over long task sequences, while our regularization keeps a rich, broad spectrum intact.
layout: 2x2 grid of histograms; columns are tasks, rows are methods; color-coded
description: A 2x2 grid of log-scale density histograms of Hessian eigenvalues. Columns are labeled Task 50 and Task 300. The top row, in blue, is standard backpropagation (BP). The bottom row, in green, is L2_ER, the proposed method. The y-axis is Density from 10^-10 to 10^2 and the x-axis is Eigenvalue from roughly 0 to 1000. At Task 50, BP shows a dense bulk near zero plus a few isolated outlier spikes out to about 750. At Task 300, BP has collapsed to a few thin spikes near zero and one near 90, so the spectrum is nearly empty. L2_ER keeps a broad bulk with a heavy tail and several outlier eigenvalues at both tasks, reaching about 500 at Task 300. The eye goes first to the contrast between the sparse blue panel at top right and the dense green panel below it.
caption: The Hessian eigenspectrum on continual Imagenet at task initialization. The top row shows the eigenspectrum on a network using standard backpropagation (BP). The bottom row shows the eigenspectrum using L2-ER regularization (ours).
abstract: We investigate why deep neural networks suffer from loss of plasticity in continual learning, and thus fail to learn new tasks without reinitializing parameters. We show that this failure is preceded by Hessian spectral collapse at new-task initialization, where meaningful curvature directions vanish and gradient descent becomes ineffective. Analyzing a linearized ReLU network, we derive explicit $Îµ$-rank conditions for successful training and prove that the loss-weighted Gram matrix is spectrally equivalent to the Generalized Gauss-Newton approximation, thereby relating NTK dynamics to Hessian curvature. Targeting spectral collapse directly, we then discuss the Kronecker factored approximation of the Hessian, which motivates two regularization enhancements: maintaining high effective feature rank and applying L2 penalties. Experiments on continual supervised and reinforcement learning tasks confirm that combining these two regularizers effectively preserves plasticity.
